acceptanceCriteria: A check fails when the number of unbounded test packages rises above a recorded ceiling.
The ten most expensive unbounded packages have declared, Landlock-enforced read scopes or a recorded reason they cannot.
Selected seconds as a share of the full suite is reported for each PR and retained.
body: Observed 2026-10-04 during a CI audit (Core 1.0.0-rc.1 build 163, Tasks build 202) at origin/main e5d47da8; hosted run https://github.com/beamfall/corvint/actions/runs/37198363933 (4 shards, 295 packages, 5635s summed package time, race steps 1924/1647/1397/1264s). Measured with installed Core build 163 on a clean clone: corvint affected --base FIRST_PARENT over the last 20 first-parent merges selected 144 to 193 of 295 Go packages, 86% to 92% of summed test time, scope UNKNOWN every time. A merge that only adds two .corvint/changes CEM files selected 147 packages: 141 UNBOUNDED_READER and 6 PATH_LITERAL_READER. The 141 unbounded units hold 4213s of 5635s; the largest are internal/testacceptance 953s, appflows 348s, companionrelease 224s, tasks/authority 206s, extevidence 194s, tasks/store 171s. So activating selection today would save about 10%. The count has grown from 103 (V1-0081) and 129 (V1-0246) to 141. Proposal: (1) a ratchet check that refuses a new test package with no declared read scope or an increase in the unbounded count; (2) bound packages in order of hosted seconds, not package count; (3) report selected seconds per PR in the step summary as an advisory shadow metric. V1-0246, V1-0081, V1-0649, V1-0634 and V1-0635 own the bounding mechanics.
title: affected: ratchet unbounded test readers; they hold 75% of CI test time and keep selection at 86% for a docs-only change
